title: Error Boundaries and Resilient UI Design knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Error Boundaries and Resilient UI Design”?
options: Error Boundaries and Resilient UI Design helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
Error Boundaries and Resilient UI Design means the browser can enforce all permissions without the backend.
Error Boundaries and Resilient UI Design removes the need for error handling, accessibility checks and tests.
Error Boundaries and Resilient UI Design should be implemented by copying a snippet without checking the Angular version.
questions.answer_key: Error Boundaries and Resilient UI Design helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.explanation: Error Boundaries and Resilient UI Design is a concept in the supplied Angular curriculum. Its correct application depends on the intended behavior, surrounding context and verification.

questions.prompt: How should a learner work with “Handling failures at feature boundaries” in this lesson?
options: Treat “Handling failures at feature boundaries” as a reason to skip the surrounding application context.
Assume “Handling failures at feature boundaries” works identically across every Angular major and runtime.
Use “Handling failures at feature boundaries” to bypass runtime validation of external or user-provided values.
Connect “Handling failures at feature boundaries” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.answer_key: Connect “Handling failures at feature boundaries” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.explanation: The PDF explicitly lists “Handling failures at feature boundaries” under Error Boundaries and Resilient UI Design. Anchor it in a small example and check the behavior rather than relying on a memorized phrase.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest verification approach for “Error Boundaries and Resilient UI Design”?
options: Treat a successful client-side render as backend authorization evidence.
Ignore a failing test if the component looks correct in one browser.
Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
Assume an SVG diagram proves the code compiled and passed tests.
questions.answer_key: Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.explanation: Verification evidence should match the running environment. Static teaching snippets are not compiler output, and frontend checks do not replace backend authorization.
